name: Eco-Socialism
summary: Eco-socialism holds that capitalism's compulsion to accumulate and grow is the root cause of ecological destruction and social exploitation, so the two crises can only be solved together by replacing it. It calls for collective, democratic control of production and democratic planning around use-value and human needs, rejects market-based fixes such as carbon trading, nuclear power and productivist socialism, and stresses solidarity with the Global South and indigenous peoples. Strategy ranges from revolutionary transformation backed by popular majorities to prefigurative local projects.
scope: The Red-Green mainstream as set out in Kovel and Löwy's Ecosocialist Manifesto (2001) and the Belem Ecosocialist Declaration (2008/09), with Marxist ecology (Foster, O'Connor, Saito) as background. It excludes Bookchin's social ecology and deep ecology as distinct strands, and the social-democratic Green New Deal as a reform program, though these are discussed in the literature. Many statements are not addressed in the programmatic texts and are inferred at low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Social provision of basic needs is part of the socialist half of the program, and care work and health are valued over commodity output.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not a focus of the texts; the Belem declaration backs labor struggles and decent work, so a higher wage floor follows, though many eco-socialists want to go past wage labor.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The declaration holds that market mechanisms cannot solve the ecological crisis and that capitalism cannot be reformed away.

public-ownership.rationale: The declaration calls for collective control of the means of production, with community-controlled energy replacing fossil fuels.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Eco-socialists treat the rich as the main beneficiaries and drivers of ecological destruction, so heavy taxation is consistent, though they aim at ending the system rather than taxing it.

unions-good.rationale: Belem says labor struggle is inseparable from environmental justice, but also asks workers to move beyond defending existing industries.

property-fundamental.rationale: Eco-socialism seeks collective control of production and restoring the commons, so private property is not an inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Immediate demands include enforceable emission cuts; yet regulation is seen as insufficient because capital must grow, so the agreement is moderate.

cut-welfare.rationale: Meeting human needs and care work is central; cutting welfare runs against the program.

worker-ownership.rationale: Self-management and workers controlling their workplaces are part of the ecosocialist economy, alongside community and public control.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not a major topic; the anti-statist, emancipatory orientation and hostility to repressive states suggest opposition.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; an anti-authoritarian left leaning suggests mild support, but adherents have no program on it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Eco-socialists oppose racism and sexism, but speech law is not addressed and the left is split on it.

strong-leader.rationale: The program rests on democratic collective decision making from below and rejects despotism.

state-harmful.rationale: Many strands are post-statist and see the capitalist state as repressive, but most want democratic political power used for transformation, not no state now.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; broad left view is for restrictions, inferred only.

empower-police-military.rationale: The declaration demands an end to war spending and criticizes militarism and imperial aggression.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed, and the left, including ecofeminists, is split.

decide-locally.rationale: Local food sovereignty, community-controlled energy and local assemblies figure prominently, though planning is also coordinated at wider scales.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; a generally emancipatory left view favours rehabilitation over punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Gender equality is integral to ecosocialism; the family is not discussed, so this is inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not mentioned; the commitment to end all forms of domination suggests support.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed directly; women's movements are hailed and gender equality is integral, so legal abortion is inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Mostly secular left, though Kovel was a Christian drawn to liberation theology and indigenous spiritual traditions are respected; no call for a larger public religious role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Ending racism and every form of domination is part of the program, notably environmental racism.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed in these texts; adherents lean toward the standard left view.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Internationalist outlook; local and indigenous cultures are valued but national tradition is not a goal.

gradual-change.rationale: The declaration demands revolutionary transformation of social and political structures, arguing reform cannot remove growth imperative.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Internationalist and anti-imperialist; stress on the Global South as victims of rich-world ecological aggression and climate displacement points against restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: They criticize institutions like the World Bank and UN climate talks as captured by capital, favoring grassroots international networks over empowering existing bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Capitalist globalization and expansion into new markets are blamed for ecological and social ruin.

nation-first.rationale: Internationalist; the climate crisis is treated as requiring global solidarity, with rich nations owing the poor.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Strong anti-imperialist and anti-war stance makes endorsement unlikely, though not directly addressed.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalism and solidarity with the South lean toward free movement, but it is not a stated demand.

limit-growth.rationale: Capitalism's Grow-or-Die imperative is the root problem, and ecosocialism prizes quality over quantity.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The declaration frames the choice as ecosocialism or barbarism and demands enforceable emissions cuts now.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Eco-socialists reject technological fixes and hold that technologies shaped by capital need transformation; social change is primary.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The declaration lists eliminating nuclear energy among immediate demands.

revolution-justified.rationale: The declaration calls for revolutionary transformation of social and political structures.

experts-over-public.rationale: Investment and technology choices are to be made democratically, not left to technocrats or enterprises.

central-planning.rationale: Democratic planning is central but is meant to be participatory; strands split between centralized and decentralized forms and reject bureaucratic command.

socialized-markets.rationale: Kovel expects markets to become unnecessary, though some strands, such as market socialist-leaning ones, tolerate limited markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not part of the program; they aim at collective control, not a single-tax reform of capitalism.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with egalitarian orientation but a minor reform.

basic-income.rationale: Not a staple of the texts; decoupling needs from work fits, but adherents are divided on it as a reform.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: They oppose free trade but also favour local food sovereignty and de-globalization on social grounds, not protection for industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Investment decisions should be taken democratically and collectively; this is closer to democratic direction than to a state elite directing capital.

widespread-small-property.rationale: They favor collective and commons ownership over spreading property among small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Use-value over exchange-value points toward ending commodity relations, but timing and means are loosely stated and strands differ.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A market-led money system is foreign to the program; democratic control of finance is the aim.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Prices and wages are not to be set by employer bodies; collective democratic planning is the model.

one-party-rule.rationale: Eco-socialists criticize Stalinism and state capitalism and call for a democratic, post-statist socialism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Rejects hierarchical rule; democratic collective control is central.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy in the economy and society is a core idea, and ecosocialism is framed as expanding democratic freedom.

direct-votes.rationale: Planning from below and assemblies favour participatory forms, though many also accept delegated councils.

workers-councils.rationale: Kovel proposes recallable, rotating councils and productive communities; Löwy draws on the Paris Commune.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; self-determination for peoples is favored but secession is not discussed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Opposes domination and hierarchy in all forms.

political-violence-never.rationale: Strategy is generally nonviolent and prefigurative, but revolution is not ruled out and Malm argues nonviolence may need to be revisited.

war-builds-character.rationale: The declaration condemns war spending and militarism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Largely secular left, though faith-inspired members exist and indigenous spiritualities are respected.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Democratic, collective lawmaking is the program; scripture has no standing.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Privatizing public functions contradicts collective control.

military-superiority.rationale: Calls for ending war spending and rejects imperial aggression.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Internationalist and committed to ending racism and domination.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rooted in Marxism and metabolic rift theory, though they add ecological and other domination to class as drivers.

equal-outcomes.rationale: They aim for meeting everyone's needs and an end to class society and exploitation.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous peoples are seen as holders of sustainable traditions and are asked to take a full part in the revolution; Kovel criticizes their removal from lands.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Kovel proposes cancelling Global South debt and funding reparations and ecologically sound development; Belem calls ecological destruction an aggression of rich on poor.

civilizational-union.rationale: Internationalism is by class and solidarity, not civilizational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Ecosocialism condemns the profit motive and puts collective needs and ecology first.

duties-before-rights.rationale: They stress collective responsibility and ecological limits but also freedom and emancipation, so duties are not placed above rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: They speak of ecological integrity and treat nature as more than a resource, though strands differ from deep ecology, which Kovel criticized.

limit-population.rationale: Eco-socialists oppose Malthusian explanations and blame class and capitalist technology, not population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Capitalist industrialism is condemned, but they do not reject industry or modern life wholesale; Belem favors reorienting production.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Saito opposes accelerationism; technology must be remade, not sped up.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; skepticism of capitalist technology suggests caution.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; opposition inferred from preference for democratic, participatory decisions.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The program texts never mention encryption or digital privacy, so adherents have no common position.

restore-past-order.rationale: They seek a new social order, not a return, and reject nostalgic conservatism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: They are programmatic and ideologically committed, rejecting piecemeal clean capitalism.

direct-action.rationale: Belem emphasizes mass action and movements, though they also work in Green parties and alliances.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative projects that build post-capitalist practices in the present are a main strategy.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Kovel criticized deep ecology and primitivism; ecosocialism is not a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Devine names abolishing the social division of labour as a principle, but it is not universal among adherents.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A needs-based economy of use-value replacing exchange-value is the core of the program.

production-for-use.rationale: Belem explicitly shifts from exchange-value to use-value.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist grounding; profit derives from exploitation of labour and of nature.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Eco-socialists criticize Stalinism and state socialism and favor a post-statist democracy.

collective-farming.rationale: They prefer local food sovereignty and agroecology, which can be cooperative or communal but are not forced collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Belem ties imperial expansion for resources and markets to capitalism and condemns war spending.

taxation-theft.rationale: Collective provision is a core idea.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; they accept restricting polluting activity but also socialize much of life, so neither side fits cleanly.

individual-rights-only.rationale: They affirm collective and commons rights and indigenous collective rights alongside individual ones.

conscription.rationale: Antimilitarist; calls for ending war spending.

state-as-business.rationale: Contradicts both democratic control and anti-commodification.

positive-liberty.rationale: Ecosocialism links freedom to meeting needs and collective control of the conditions of life.

media-academia-power.rationale: They see corporate and capital power as dominant, not media and academia.

hereditarian-race.rationale: They oppose racism and ground differences in social conditions.

organic-representation.rationale: Rejects corporatist forms; wants democratic councils and assemblies.

total-state.rationale: Criticizes bureaucratic collectivism and state capitalism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Internationalist, with no nationalist rebirth theme.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Eco-socialists criticize capitalist science and technology, but some, like Foster, defend scientific realism; split.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist tradition is skeptical of universal moral truths but eco-socialists make strong ethical claims.

single-common-good.rationale: They frame a common ecological and social interest against capital, but also stress pluralism of struggles; split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; the internationalist anti-imperialist left is generally critical, and the topic is contested within it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora citizenship rights are not addressed in eco-socialist texts and adherents have no shared line.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival as a state project does not appear in eco-socialist programs, so no position is stated.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control of production and investment decisions is a central demand.

school-vouchers.rationale: Privatizing public education is contrary to collective provision.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; austerity is opposed in the declaration's call for full employment and public investment, though stimulus for growth is also doubted.

economic-freedom.rationale: They reject market freedom as the basis of liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: The texts rely on democratic institutions and mass movements, and say nothing about rulers' moral example as a basis of government.

national-self-determination.rationale: Support for oppressed peoples and Global South struggles implies it, though internationalists qualify national frames.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Mostly secular but some adherents, like Kovel, are religious; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Internationalist solidarity opposes dividing welfare by citizenship.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Meeting needs and valuing care work contradict conditional workfare.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rooted in Marxism and rejects reform of capitalism by partnership with capital.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Values education, arts and culture, and opposes productivist destructiveness.

dominated-front.rationale: They back anti-imperialist solidarity but not a state-level front per se.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gender equality is integral to ecosocialism.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; critique of finance is strong but no legal ban on interest is on the agenda.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist heritage views the capitalist state as serving capital and as repressive, though the more strategic strands see political power as a lever.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Fossil fuels are to be replaced by community-controlled renewables.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Opposes domination and values cultural plurality and internationalism.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy view alien to its class-based analysis and anti-racism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Red-Green parties generally favor it, but it is not a core demand.

national-mission.rationale: Imperialist expansion is condemned in the Belem declaration, so a national mission to export a system is rejected.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: They name gender equality as integral and gender domination as part of the structures to end.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Belem criticizes elite capture of climate diplomacy by corporations and the World Bank.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Opposed to coercive population control and discrimination.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; opposes repression, so accountability is inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Collective control of the economy and care work is central.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Ending racism and all forms of domination is part of the program, so discouraging mixed marriage is rejected.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Ending all forms of domination presupposes equal worth and rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: They stress global character of ecological crisis and internationalist strategy, but the thesis is not discussed.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial and indigenous-aligned orientation suggests agreement, though not stated.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between equal-law and minority-rights concerns.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Anti-authoritarian and not concerned with restricting religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; agroecology and animal welfare views vary.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Post-statist outlook and criticism of Stalinism contradict strengthening states.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Democratic mandate matters: transformation should have majority popular support, per the declaration.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is a capitalist expansion strategy they oppose.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not libertarian; revolutionary change is justified and they accept collective restrictions.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; split between anti-fascist bans and civil libertarian views.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-domination is a unifying theme, from Bookchin through to Belem.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; they favor councils and assemblies over checks-and-balances design.

vanguard-party.rationale: They criticize Stalinism and favor grassroots, prefigurative organizing and movement alliances over a vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Environmentalism of the poor and Global South priority are central; social justice is inseparable from ecology.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Favors collective and public ownership over sell-off of public housing.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Eco-socialists explicitly oppose Malthusian explanations in favor of class injustice.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rotating and recallable councils are proposed, but lottery is not stated.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Anti-authoritarian and critical of repressive states.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; compatible with prioritizing needs over markets.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Fits Paris Commune inspiration drawn by Löwy; not explicitly stated.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; democratic centralist versus pluralist strands differ.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: They distrust the EU as a neoliberal project yet favor international cooperation; split.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; the anti-hierarchy outlook leans against.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Antiwar and internationalist, but the revolutionary defeatist line is not a stated eco-socialist position.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Values arts and culture and opposes repression.

recall-officials.rationale: Kovel proposes recallable councils and Löwy invokes the Commune.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Demand to end war spending and criticism of imperial aggression imply opposition to permanent military blocs.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Favors collective and public provision over universal home ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: Commune tradition suggests militia, but not addressed in eco-socialist programs.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Saito does not reject urban life; local agroecology is favored but no moral hierarchy.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Education is valued and the program is not populist anti-intellectual.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not addressed in eco-socialist texts, and internationalists are not engaged by it.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Respect for indigenous traditions and anti-racism suggest agreement, though not stated.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality is integral; not addressed on schooling.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Foster and Burkett ground their case in scientific ecology.

minority-language-support.rationale: Respect for indigenous and local cultures suggests support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law for religious minorities are not discussed, and adherents are divided between rights and equal-law concerns.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Liberation from domination is central, but not addressed in these terms.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Kovel proposes cancelling Global South debt; Belem frames ecological destruction as rich countries' aggression.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: They link anti-imperialism to transforming economic structures, treating the Global South as first victim of capitalism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Kovel proposes interim assemblies, but constituent assemblies as such are not addressed.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: They reject growth as a goal and productivist authoritarianism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Environmental destruction is an act of aggression by the rich against the poor; Kovel proposes reparations.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Calls for eliminating nuclear energy and war spending; nuclear weapons are repugnant.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The mode of electing a head of state is not addressed in eco-socialist texts.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Prices and finance should be under democratic control, not insulated technocracy.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Collective control and commons aim at serving social and ecological needs.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Eco-socialists criticize Stalinism, bureaucratic collectivism and state capitalism; though some call it deformed socialism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: They demand action before the crisis worsens and oppose risky technologies such as nuclear and GM crops.

collective-defense.rationale: Opposes military blocs and war spending.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations are not addressed in the program texts, and adherents hold mixed secular and faith-inspired views.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: favors democratic structures over ceremonial heads.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special-autonomy arrangements for regions are not addressed in eco-socialist texts.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Marxist tradition and Barry Commoner stress social conditions, and capitalism manufactures wants.

space-expansion.rationale: Unlimited expansion contradicts the ecological limits and it wastes resources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian democracy is preferred to mixed rule.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed in eco-socialist programs, so no position is stated.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not addressed; Maoist thesis not a typical eco-socialist position, though they critique bureaucratic restoration.

land-redistribution.rationale: Local food sovereignty and soil renewal imply support for peasants' access to land, but not explicitly.

refugee-return.rationale: Internationalist and sympathetic to the displaced; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing leaving a religion contradicts the anti-authoritarian, emancipatory stance of the program.

women-must-cover.rationale: Gender equality is integral to ecosocialism.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed in program texts, and the left is split over the euro.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Internationalism is class and solidarity-based, not kin-based.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government within a state is not addressed in eco-socialist texts.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy between emigration and local struggle is not addressed in eco-socialist texts.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Foster and Saito read Marx's materialism as central, via metabolic rift.

ban-cartels.rationale: They want to end concentrated capital through collective control, not preserve competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: They oppose rescuing capitalist firms but want public ownership rather than collapse; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial review versus majority rule is not addressed in eco-socialist texts, and adherents are split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender equality is integral; quotas not addressed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: They favor local food sovereignty but not autarkic imperial blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: They reject free trade as it stands; binding standards fit but are seen as insufficient.

moral-incentives.rationale: Shift toward values of care, quality and social duty over exchange-value; not an explicit program.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Belem relies on mass action and majority support, not small armed groups.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Capitalism's competitive Grow-or-Die imperative is identified as the cause of ecological ruin; the program is built on cooperation and democratic planning.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Eco-socialism is internationalist and stresses solidarity with the Global South and indigenous peoples, so a nation-centred curriculum is disfavoured. Inferred; the texts do not address schooling.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Belem declaration condemns imperialism and colonial domination and defends the self-determination of the Global South.

patriotic-education.rationale: Internationalist and critical of nationalism; schooling for national pride is not part of the program. Inferred at low confidence.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Eco-socialists stress justice for indigenous and oppressed groups and are unlikely to abolish remedial measures; the texts say little on admissions, so inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Kovel and the program call for democratic control of investment and finance and criticise debt and banks; public money creation is inferred from that, not stated.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Eco-socialism holds that capitalism's compulsion to accumulate drives ecological and social crisis that it cannot escape, so it cannot adapt indefinitely.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The program rejects imperialism and great-power domination and favours solidarity with the Global South. Inferred as applied to a former empire.

delink-world-market.rationale: The program opposes capitalist globalisation and backs local and sovereign alternatives, but also stresses international solidarity and planning; adherents differ on delinking. Not stated.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The program stresses a common working-class struggle with the poor of the Global South, though some Marxist strands note rich-country privilege and consumption. Inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Eco-socialism rejects both property rights as absolute and racial and gender oppression (the Belem declaration names gender equality), so it would back anti-discrimination law.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Eco-socialists defend rights but favour democratic majorities and collective control over entrenched limits; the texts do not address it, so split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the Belem declaration's anti-imperialism and support for indigenous and Global South self-determination; borders drawn by colonial powers are not defended.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the program's call for democratic control of society; hereditary rule is incompatible with it.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from its majoritarian democratic planning model; a single member's veto would block collective ecological decisions, though indigenous consent carries weight.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the movement's revolutionary-democratic tradition, which accepts removing rulers who betray popular mandates.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from its preference for popular, democratic institutions over monarchy; the texts do not address the question directly.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from ecological ethics that extend concern to nonhuman life; Kovel and others criticise factory farming as a product of capital.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from its critique of industrial agriculture and capital's treatment of nature; adherents are split on abolition versus humane use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from its demand for structural change and collective ownership rather than charity from the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Belem declaration calls for active struggle and political organisation, so withdrawing from public affairs is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist critique of commodity culture and consumerism as sustaining capitalist growth.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist tradition it draws on, which includes hegemony through culture and institutions alongside coercion.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Belem declaration blames capitalist imperialism for transferring wealth from the Global South and demands repayment of ecological debt.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and solidarity with migrants and the Global South.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from the socialist tradition's rejection of Stalinist direction and its stress on national and local democratic paths.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from its call for debt cancellation, reparations and ecological debt owed to the South, with emphasis on food sovereignty rather than aid-free autarky.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and rejection of nationalist territorial claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The declaration backs indigenous rights and leadership in struggles but not political rule over other citizens; this is inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from the Red-Green left's broad anti-fascist commitments.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from its critique of Stalinism, balanced by a rejection of equating socialism with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist historiography it draws on, which treats slavery as the central cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from its solidarity with indigenous and oppressed peoples, who are often the targets of such monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from the program's focus on women's oppression and gender equality over parity programmes for men.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the program's feminist analysis of gendered violence as asymmetrical.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from its universalist, democratic program; the texts stress anti-imperial self-determination, so adherents are somewhat split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from its democratic, anti-militarist stance.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from its valuing of care and reproduction over commodity output, and from socialist-feminist politics.

missingStatements.text: Reducing material production and consumption in rich countries is needed to stay within ecological limits.
missingStatements.rationale: Belem prioritizes quality over quantity and rejects productivism, and Saito and Kovel argue for sufficiency and degrowth in the rich world.

missingStatements.text: Carbon trading and other market mechanisms cannot solve the climate crisis.
missingStatements.rationale: Belem condemns cap-and-trade and the Clean Development Mechanism as turning the atmosphere into a commodity for polluters.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow policy instrument (carbon markets); the stance is captured by limit-growth, drastic-climate-action and markets-allocate-better.

missingStatements.text: Production and investment should be decided through democratic planning rather than by firms, investors and banks.
missingStatements.rationale: Belem names democratic planning of production and exchange and democratic control of investment as its core economic demand.

missingStatements.text: Private cars and trucks should be replaced by free public transport.
missingStatements.rationale: Belem's program replaces private cars and trucks with free public transit and rail.
missingStatements.declined: A specific transport policy, too narrow for a bank every audit must answer; broader stances are covered by public-ownership and drastic-climate-action.

notes: Strands differ: Saito stresses degrowth and local cooperatives, others (Löwy, Tanuro) democratic centralised planning and a Green New Deal style program; Bookchin's communalism is post-statist. Many answers on cultural and institutional statements are inferred.
